title: Godzilla Minus one was by far the better movie about the AtomBomb released this year.

It’s about this guys life and his most significant achievement happens to be the atom bomb. It explores his psyche and how he emotionally responded to being the creator of such a weapon. I think you're comparing films that have two very different perspectives its drawing from.

Oppenheimer is a very personal study about his own guilt of creating for creating the bomb and the fallout it created for himself and the rest of the world. The country considers him a hero for winning the war, even though it meant nuking civilian populations, but he cannot escape his own demons that torment him for his role in killing hundreds of thousands and ushering in a new age of potential worldwide destruction. It's more concerned with the burden of responsibility, hubris, ego and naivety of trying to stay neutral in a situation where doing so means being complicit.

Godzilla Minus One focuses on rebuilding a country that was annihilated and it's people coming together to build something new in the wake of such horrible destruction. It deals with the some of the same subject matter but its telling a different story with different intentions. These characters come together to protect what is left, build a new future and move on from their own trauma to forge a better world.

They make a fun double feature but I don't think they're comparable in the way you are comparing them.

> For one, i think Oppenheimer was pretty vapid in its treatment of americas deployment nukes and the moral questions that stem from it 

I see that you dismiss it as "cheesy" — and fair enough, though "cheesy" is not particularly useful criticism — but the last line of the movie — the revelation that the entire movie has been building to — is that Oppenheimer realizes too late that developing the atomic bomb has doomed the world. He has personally morally damned himself, which explains a lot of his behavior throughout the rest of the movie, especially after the bomb. 

Oppenheimer as shown in the movie is a man who thought he was doing something morally neutral, perhaps even morally good — creating a bomb that he believed would be created anyway, and doing it to defeat the Nazis. As it turned out, the bomb wasn't necessary to defeat the Nazis, the Nazis weren't close to creating a bomb themselves, and Oppenheimer saw that the moral calculations about using the bomb were simplistic at best. 

*Oppenheimer* takes as a given that creating the bomb was not a good thing, and is more interested in exploring why that particular man decided to take on that job, and how it affected him. I can understand people who think it lets him off the hook, or don't like Nolan's methods, but it's not a movie "about" the bomb, partly because I don't see anything in it that argues in the slightest that the bomb was worth it.

I really wish people could just talk about why they enjoyed a film without feeling the need to denigrate another (especially when the connection between the two is, in this case, quite a stretch).

This is a truly bizarre comparison. While nukes figure incidentally into both films, neither movie is *about* the a-bomb.

One is a character study about a controversial historical figure, and the other is a sci-fi monster movie that explores anxiety, struggle, and perseverance in post-war Japan. 

Godzilla being a metaphor for the a-bomb (and, according to the film’s director, a lot of other things) is merely context. It’s not what the movie is about.

Fetishizing? Did you watch the film? Did you miss the parts where he's facing the guilt of developing the bomb immediately after it's dropped. 

The entire test sequence in the desert is there to objectively portray the extreme destructive power of the bomb.

And to say the film is all about the bomb when the actual dropping on Japan isn't even depicted, but his immediate reaction is depicted instead. I mean come on.

If you thought Oppenheimer was a pro-war film I can't think you have even basic critical thought.
